fullAnalysis: Puzzle #682 opens with Ball-jointed, Bobblehead, Voodoo, Russian nesting (Matryoshka), and Barbie, a set of clues that appear to belong to completely different categories on first read. That spread is what makes the board deceptive: instead of pointing toward a single subject area, the clues push you toward toys, brands, folklore, or everyday vocabulary all at once. When Pinpoint does this, the safer move is to stop grouping by topic and start testing whether the same missing word can complete every clue naturally.

That approach resolves this board quickly. The shared connector is doll. Once you test doll across the full list, each phrase settles into a clean compound and the noise disappears. The answer "Types of doll" works because it explains every clue with the same exact pattern, not because one or two clues feel loosely related. If one connector completes all five without stretching the meaning, that is usually the correct Pinpoint solution.
solutionNarrative: I looked for the fastest anchor first and used Barbie as my test case. Once I had a candidate connector in mind, I checked whether the same missing word could complete the other clues without changing the meaning or forcing an awkward phrase. That is the quickest way to handle boards that mix several different surface categories.

For #682, the connector doll held up across the entire set, so the answer "Types of doll" became much easier to trust. I then ran back through the board clue by clue to make sure the pattern stayed natural, common, and exact. When every clue resolves cleanly under the same shared word, the final answer is usually ready to lock in.
